analysis.title: Viewpoint by Charts – November 2026
key_insights: CIO expects the recycling and risk-off period to end once Q4 corporate guidance and FY 2027 outlooks unfold and the mid-term elections conclude, with focus shifting to solid growth, record margins and rising productivity, even as the economy inches closer to mid-cycle.
Possible supports for a year-end rally: solid EPS growth, strong demand for 5%+ Treasury yields, moderating speculation and emerging AI-adoption stories.

CIO says recent market weakness may be overdone and sees potential opportunities in semiconductors, power, Financials, Healthcare, Defense, software and cybersecurity. Attractive yields and elevated commodities are contrasted with ongoing Real Estate challenges.

US Q3 2026 GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace, the strongest in a year. Nominal growth is running above the 10-year Treasury yield, which CIO reads as a stronger nominal growth regime rather than a loss of confidence in US credit.
CIO stays overweight Equities with a preference for the US, and treats noise-driven pullbacks as chances to buy or rebalance.

CIO is constructive on Fixed Income but underweight to fund the Equity overweight. With the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% and real yields above 2.5%, it favors moving out of cash and the front end of the curve to extend duration.
Thematic opportunities named: biotechnology, life sciences, robotics, AI-enabled infrastructure, grid modernization, power generation, and aerospace and defense.

S&P 500 blended net profit margin for Q3 2026 is set to be 14.9%, among the highest since 2010. Seven sectors report margins above their 5-year averages and five report quarter-over-quarter increases.
CIO argues AI opportunity may increasingly favor adopters, meaning companies that turn AI into productivity gains, and that broader adoption may support higher-for-longer margins.

Hyperscalers have issued $272B of debt in 2026, up from $108B in 2025. Credit-spread widening has stayed concentrated in AI-related issuers rather than the broader investment-grade market, and CIO calls the underperformance primarily technical, with patience warranted.
In Alternatives, CIO favors Venture Capital and Growth Equity for early-stage innovation, as the average US company waited 14 years to IPO in 2025 versus 8 years in 2000 (PitchBook).

Scenario odds: bull 25%, base 55%, bear 15%, grizzly 5%. The base case has GDP momentum holding, the oil and gas price surge not turning into economy-wide inflation, limited hikes later in the year or a rate pause, and double-digit S&P 500 earnings growth in 2026.

sector_views.rationale: CIO sees recent weakness as possibly overdone, with opportunity in semiconductors and AI-enabled infrastructure. The bull case has AI capex accelerating and lifting Technology.
CIO names power as a potential opportunity and cites grid modernization and power generation investment flows.
CIO lists Financials among sectors with potential opportunities after the pullback.
CIO lists Healthcare among potential opportunities and cites biotechnology and life sciences as themes.
CIO cites heavy investment flows into aerospace and defense and lists Defense among potential opportunities.
CIO lists software and cybersecurity among potential opportunities after recent weakness.
CIO cites ongoing Real Estate challenges.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 blended Q3 2026 net profit margin set to be 14.9% (FactSet, as of Oct 26, 2026), among the highest since 2010, with forward consensus estimates pointing to continued strength.
Seven sectors report Q3 2026 net profit margins above their 5-year averages and five report a quarter-over-quarter increase.
The CIO base case has S&P 500 earnings growth at double-digit percentages or higher in 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Strongest growth in a year. Nominal growth is above the 10-year yield, which supports the view that higher yields reflect resilience and not a credit-confidence problem.
CIO calls all-in yields compelling and favors extending duration.
Supports the case for adding Fixed Income exposure.
Blended figure, still being updated as reports come in. Among the highest since 2010.

risk_factors: AI capital investment peaking and then falling, which would hit earnings and Technology.
Stagflation worries, with a growth slump alongside inflation well above target and rate-hike expectations rising.
Recession odds rising alongside midterm concerns, with fiscal spending dropping and the consumer pulling back.
Credit stress in lower-quality credits spreading to high-quality credit.
Hyperscaler debt issuance and softer technicals widening credit spreads further in AI-related issuers.
vol_and_positioning: CIO cites cautious investor positioning as a support for markets.
CIO notes moderating speculation as a possible support for a year-end rally.
geopolitical: The year-end rally case assumes geopolitical risks ease.
Bull case: geopolitical tensions ease significantly and peace accelerates.
Base case: Middle East tensions ease considerably.
Bear case: geopolitical tensions re-escalate and trade wars develop again and stick.
Grizzly case: geopolitical tensions boil over into broader conflict.

tension_points.bull_case: AI capital investment accelerates and lifts Technology again, with a more measured buildout, broader adoption and earnings growth supporting markets.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capital investment peaks and begins to drop, earnings decline and technology bubble concerns materialize, with defensive areas outperforming.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI capital investment peaking and beginning to drop would invalidate the bull thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher yields reflect stronger nominal growth, with 3.4% Q3 GDP and nominal growth above the 10-year yield supporting the sustainability of government debt.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising yields could reflect mounting fiscal pressures and a loss of confidence in US credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fiscal spending drop and consumer pullback that turn growth into a slump while inflation stays well above target would break the resilience read.

theme_stances.key_argument: Q4 guidance, FY 2027 outlooks and the end of the mid-term elections should end the risk-off period and refocus markets on growth, margins and productivity.
With 10-year yields near 5% and real yields above 2.5%, all-in yields are compelling and investors should move out of cash and the front end.
